causes.text: In July 2022, Walmart announced it was purchasing 4,500 electric delivery vehicles from startup Canoo to build out its own last-mile delivery network. The retailer also highlighted that its internal Spark platform already handled 75% of deliveries, underscoring a strategic push to control its own logistics. DoorDash was not mentioned in this announcement, which indicated Walmart's decreasing reliance on third-party providers.

source_info.title: Walmart purchases Canoo electric vehicles to expand delivery network

effects.text: On August 19, 2022, DoorDash sent Walmart a 30-day notice to terminate their four-year delivery partnership and publicly confirmed that it would end the arrangement. DoorDash explained that the partnership was no longer mutually beneficial and said it would focus on its Marketplace and Platform offerings, including testing a new service with Meta's Facebook Marketplace.

source_info.title: DoorDash ends partnership with Walmart and pivots to new partners like Meta

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Walmart's investment in 4,500 electric delivery vehicles signaled a commitment to build its own logistics network and reduce dependence on third-party delivery services. By highlighting that its Spark platform already accounted for 75% of deliveries, Walmart demonstrated that it could internalize its e-commerce fulfillment at scale.

As Walmart ramped up its own delivery capabilities, the economic rationale for outsourcing deliveries to DoorDash weakened. Industry analysts noted that Walmart's greater control over last-mile logistics would allow it to lower costs and improve service reliability. This shift reduced the volume of orders routed through third-party platforms.

DoorDash responded by sending Walmart a 30-day termination notice and publicly ending their partnership. Influenced by the news, DoorDash's stock price fell by about 3.3% during the day and closed down about 2.6%, reflecting investors' concerns about the termination of the cooperation and future order flow.

rationale: Walmart's decision to invest heavily in its own delivery fleet and highlight its internal Spark platform reduced its dependence on DoorDash. Recognizing that continuing the partnership would yield diminishing returns, DoorDash opted to exit and redeploy resources toward other partnerships like Meta's Facebook Marketplace.
counterfactual_analysis: If Walmart had not built out its own delivery infrastructure, the partnership might have continued, and DoorDash would not have needed to seek new collaborations. In that scenario, DoorDash's focus on B2B offerings such as DoorDash Drive may have been less urgent.

adversarial_confounders.text: Operational challenges or customer service issues within the DoorDash-Walmart collaboration could have prompted the breakup independent of Walmart's logistics expansion.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Such internal factors might also explain the partnership's end, weakening the causal link to Walmart's vehicle purchase.

details.commentary: Instacart's confidential filing signaled that another scaled player was moving toward the public markets in local delivery and grocery. Investors anticipated tougher rivalry for merchants, shoppers and advertising dollars, which could pressure DoorDash's margins and growth in adjacent categories.

details.pestel_factor: Economic - Investor appetite for multiple delivery platforms
details.commentary: A window for tech IPOs allowed more delivery platforms to seek separate listings and capital access. The prospect of Instacart joining the public peer set reminded investors that market share and unit economics would be contested, tempering enthusiasm for DoorDash's valuation.
